title: Janus config backup — providers, agent keys, router config
description: Portable, environment-independent config export for the Janus LLM gateway. Secrets stay encrypted (JSEC ciphertext / HMAC hashes pass through); DB-internal ids never appear — every cross-reference is a natural key (provider name, model name, key hash). Convention follows the published-schema pattern of omp (canonical $id + optional $schema self-reference in documents, e.g. oh-my-pi's mcp-schema.json) and the pi/omp providers-keys-router config triad. See docs/CONFIG-BACKUP.md.

$schema.description: Optional self-reference to this schema's canonical $id (editor autocomplete/validation), per the omp published-schema convention. Exporters SHOULD write it. EXCLUDED from payload_sha256 (like 'integrity') so editors may add/remove it freely.

version.description: Format version. Checked by the lenient pre-read (numeric >1 incl. floats → unsupported_version; bools excluded explicitly — Python isinstance(True, int) is True); this const runs only after it. Integral floats (1.0) pass via JSON Schema numeric equality.

taken_at.description: UTC export time, RFC 3339 (e.g. 2026-10-13T03:15:00Z). Validators MUST enable format assertion (format is annotation-only by default in 2020-12).

host.description: Source host label (informational only; never gates restore). EXCLUDED from payload_sha256 (like 'integrity' and '$schema') — strip it before sharing a document off-host (C10) without breaking integrity.

schema_migrations.description: Applied schema_migrations versions at export time. REQUIRED and non-empty: absent/empty is schema_invalid (400). Restore compares the payload-derived required set against the TARGET's applied migrations (target lagging → migration_pending); this list feeds the lead warning (target ahead) and forensics.

dashboard_version.description: Dashboard git sha or image tag at export time (informational).

key_ids.description: DERIVED by the exporter from the actual providers[].keys[].key_id values, sorted ascending. Restore preflight re-derives the set from the payload and requires exact equality (both directions — a stale or trimmed list is schema_invalid), then trial-decrypts EVERY provider-key envelope against the target keyring.

canary.description: Standard padded base64 (RFC 4648, +/ alphabet) of the raw bytes. JSEC envelope of the constant 'janus-config-backup-canary-v1', encrypted with the source's ACTIVE key (canary_key_id). Preflight decrypts it AND asserts plaintext == constant; a canary failure is a WARNING (the source's active key may legitimately be absent from a rotated target keyring) — the authoritative gate is the per-envelope trial-decrypt. Minted fresh per export (random GCM nonce); with no writes in between, two exports of an unchanged config differ ONLY in taken_at, canary, payload_sha256 (C3). Minted BEFORE the hash is computed; the hash covers it.

canary_key_id.description: The envelope key id the canary was sealed with (source's active key at export). Preflight decrypts the canary with exactly this id — no guessing on rotated keyrings.

hash_encoding.description: Encoding of the key_hash_b64 rows (not of the hex pepper_canary_hash).

pepper_canary_hash.description: SHA256('janus-pepper-canary-v1' || JANUS_API_KEY_PEPPER), hex — same convention as scripts/lib/janus_backup_common.sh. Restore refuses agent_keys when the target pepper's canary differs (pepper_mismatch), unless allow_foreign_keys=1 skips the section entirely.

providers.description: Sorted by name. Empty array is valid (exports no providers).

agent_keys.description: Sorted by key_hash_b64 (the row identity). Hashes only — plaintext agent keys are unrecoverable by design.

models.description: Bound public model names, sorted by name.

routes.description: model_routes rows, sorted by (model, provider) — the identity slot (the live DB's PRIMARY KEY (model_id, provider_id)).

auto_router.description: settings.auto_router value verbatim; null when never configured. v1: null sections are SKIPPED on restore in both merge and replace modes (never reset to defaults).

auto_router_reorder.description: settings.auto_router_reorder knob value verbatim; null when never configured (defaults apply). Same skip-on-null rule as auto_router.

payload_sha256.description: SHA256 hex of the canonical JSON (sort_keys, separators=(',',':'), ensure_ascii=False — same convention as app/auto_router_rules.canonical) of the whole document with 'integrity', '$schema' AND 'host' removed. Verification recomputes over the PARSED document re-serialized canonically (never over raw bytes; numbers rely on same-process shortest-repr round-trip). Computed AFTER the canary is minted — the hash covers crypto.canary. Guards ACCIDENTAL corruption only; it is unkeyed and is not tamper-evidence.

allow_internal.description: SSRF break-glass flag. Restore treats a true value as an audited break-glass write (same as the Providers page).

keys.description: May be empty — a provider with zero keys is legal (create_provider allows it). Merge identity is the exact ciphertext bytes (provider_keys has no narrower natural key); key_id is NOT an identity. Sorted by secret_ciphertext_b64 (deterministic export).

listings.description: provider_models rows (name/enabled/modality only — the pass-through 'meta' column is deliberately excluded; sync re-populates it). Sorted by name.

key_id.description: The stable JSEC envelope key id — NOT the dashboard display label 'kid#rowid'. Preflight rejects a payload where the same key_id carries ciphertext that does not decrypt under that id.

weight.description: No DB CHECK on the live fleet (verified); restore never re-imposes the page's ≥1 rule — a weight-0 row restores as 0 (with a plan warning).

secret_ciphertext_b64.description: Standard padded base64 (RFC 4648, +/ alphabet) of the raw bytes. JSEC envelope bytes, base64. Pass-through: export never decrypts, restore never re-encrypts. Preflight trial-decrypts EVERY envelope (documents are tens of KB — full coverage is cheap), so a corrupt or mislabeled envelope fails before any write. Duplicate ciphertext bytes within ONE provider are rejected (duplicate_secret); the same bytes across DIFFERENT providers only warn (a shared physical key is weird but legal). Note: the same plaintext secret encrypted on two hosts yields different envelopes (random nonce) — cross-host merge accumulates such key pairs by design (idempotent per ciphertext, not per plaintext).

prefix.description: Display/debug label only — NOT unique, NOT identity. Identity is key_hash_b64.

key_hash_b64.description: 32-byte HMAC-SHA256 digest, base64 (44 chars, one '=' pad — the pattern pins the length). Row identity on merge-restore (matches the api_keys_key_hash_uidx unique index).

created_at.description: null = no preference. For NEW rows the file value is kept when present; on a hash-match against an existing row, the DB's existing created_at is preserved and the file value is ignored (all other mutable fields upsert).

rpm_limit.description: Optional in the schema; the exporter ALWAYS emits it (null when unset). Restore: INSERT ⇒ column default; hash-match UPDATE: present-null writes NULL (the file means unlimited); an ABSENT field preserves the DB value (defensive — a conforming exporter never omits it).

tpm_limit.description: Optional in the schema; the exporter ALWAYS emits it (null when unset). Restore: INSERT ⇒ column default; hash-match UPDATE: present-null writes NULL (the file means unlimited); an ABSENT field preserves the DB value (defensive — a conforming exporter never omits it).

daily_token_limit.description: Optional in the schema; the exporter ALWAYS emits it (null when unset). Restore: INSERT ⇒ column default; hash-match UPDATE: present-null writes NULL (the file means unlimited); an ABSENT field preserves the DB value (defensive — a conforming exporter never omits it).

model_names.description: Grant list, sorted ascending. EMPTY = unrestricted (all models) — the gateway semantics, not an omission. janus-auto is never grantable (dashboard rejects it on write; migration 022 stripped it on migrate) — this is a code-verified invariant, not a schema whim. Orphan names (naming no current surface item) are LEGAL and round-trip warn-and-keep (parity with the live Keys page). Restore preflight validates non-orphan names against the post-write agent-visible surface (bound models ∪ provider listings).

name.description: Bound public model name; the virtual model (janus-auto) is never a bound model.

model.description: Bound model name; never the virtual model (janus-auto).

upstream_model_id.description: Listing name on the provider; null = the bound model's own name. A plain FIELD of the route, NOT part of its identity: route identity is the (model, provider) slot (the live PRIMARY KEY). File-vs-target divergence on this field ⇒ UPDATE + plan warning; two file routes into one (model, provider) slot (in ANY upstream form, incl. null vs own-name) ⇒ preflight duplicate_name. Absent ≡ null (normalized before compare).

priority.description: Ordering weight; no DB CHECK exists (verified via a live pg describe) — any integer passes through.

judge_model.description: null = judge DISABLED (preflight skips the surface check entirely). Non-null must be in the post-write agent-visible surface (not restricted to bound models); restore reuses the PUT /api/settings/auto-router surface check, which already handles the openai_decisions exclusion.

tiers.description: Members must be mutually exclusive across tiers and bound on Router — restore re-validates both (same rule as PUT /api/settings/auto-router).

markers.description: Trigger phrases — semantically a SET: exported sorted ascending, compared set-equal (C3/C14); re-hash may sort them.

tier_failover_enabled.description: Optional (D11). After key failover exhausts, try the next model in the same janus-auto tier (pre-commit only). Default false when omitted; gateway default off.

tier_failover_max_names.description: Optional (D11). Cap distinct same-tier names attempted per client request. Default 3 when omitted; gateway clamps to [1, 8].

judge_backend.description: Judge pipeline selector. local = kev sidecar at local_judge.endpoint; restore reuses the gateway's PUT validation (loopback-only endpoint enforced there).

local_judge.description: Local judge sidecar settings (artifact pinning, loopback endpoint, inflight cap). Null = section never configured; v1 restore skips null sections.

media_token_allowance.description: Extra token budget allowance per media part before a request leaves the fast tier.

max_media_parts.description: Media parts above this count skip the judge (fast tier).
